utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanisic and Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we begin in the usual manner by taking today's appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. It's Matthew Olmsted and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Slobodan Cvijetic and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, I assume that there is nothing to delay our -- there are no preliminary matters that we need concern ourselves with?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we're ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you take the solemn declaration, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. Could you begin by giving us your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Can you -- can you hear me now? Is this any better?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you begin by telling us your name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Ibro Osmanovic. I'm born on 5th of August, 1965 in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Worker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Have you testified previously before there this Tribunal or in any trial in your country of residence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I testified before this court four times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So you need only -- I need only remind you of the procedure. In terms of your being called as a witness by one side, in this case the Prosecution would begin by asking questions of you, and then there would be an opportunity for counsel for each of the accused to ask you questions if they wish. After re-examination by the Prosecution, the Chamber may have questions of you. You are being called under our expedited procedure having regard to the fact that you would have testified previously, which means that the Prosecution would not use as much time with as you may have experienced the first time you testified. And with that in mind, I would invite counsel for the Prosecution to begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I believe you have mentioned that you have testified several times before this Tribunal. Did you testify in the Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And prior to testifying here today, did you have the opportunity to listen to your testimony in that case?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Was that audiorecording that you listened to an accurate reflection of your testimony in that case?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions today that you were asked during your Krajisnik testimony, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: If the answers -- the answers would be the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, did you also have an opportunity to review your written statements from 10 October, 1994; 11 October, 1995; and 7 June, 2001, prior to testifying here today?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And upon review of the 10 October 1994 statement, did you have some minor typographical corrections to that statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just typos.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours I'm going ask my Case Manager to bring up on sanction 65 ter 10287.06. This is a statement that the witness created yesterday during proofing with regard to typographical errors in his October 1994 statement. Given the short time-frame, we weren't able to load it into e-court. It still needs to be translated, and we will get that done as soon as possible after this witness testifies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, if you look at the screen, is this the witness statement that contains your corrections to your 10 October 1994 statement? Perhaps you could turn to page 2?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, with these corrections, are you satisfied that the information contained in your written statements is accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time we would move to admit the 92 ter package of this witness, including this last statement with the corrections that we just reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P1041.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Osmanovic, we've just addressed some preliminary matters. Now I get so ask you some clarifying questions with regard to your prior testimony and your prior statements. And I would like to begin, first with -- in your Krajisnik testimony, around page 5225. You mentioned that after the Serbs took over the town of Vlasenica, the Muslims were required to turn in their fire-arms. Could you tell us how this instruction, this order was conveyed to the Muslim population in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim population in Vlasenica heard this message from a Volkswagen Golf vehicle which had a megaphone on the roof and circulated around town informing the Muslim population of Vlasenica municipality that they should turn over all legally and illegally owned weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: To whom did that Golf vehicle belong?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The police station of Vlasenica, otherwise called the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And where were the Muslims supposed to turn in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The neighbourhood where I lived turned over their weapons at the perimeter of the hospital. People who lived close to the police station turned over their weapons at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now at these collection points, were there any police officers present?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 2281 on the screen, please. And the witness will mark something on this photograph with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look at the photograph that's in front of you. Could you tell us, what is this building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the building of the public security station in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Is this how the SJB building looked back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: This was in 1992. After the war, another floor was built on top, and it was painted blue. This is how the building looked in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the interior layout of the SJB building back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And how did you become familiar with the interior of this building prior to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was also the Fire Brigade Society in this building. They occupied two offices and one conference rooming on one floor. The police was on the other floor. On the ground floor, there were the offices of the Fire Brigade Society, and there were fire vehicles parked outside and their equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, just for the record, were you a member of that fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for many years.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can you tell us where was the office of the chief of police located in this building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The office of the chief of police was on the second floor, this window here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just for the record, the witness marked it with a red pen. I think he put a bit of a scribble on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And we'd like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P1042.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to 22 May 1992, the second time you were arrested by the police. In your testimony, and in your written statement, you state that the police arrested you, brought you to the SJB building, and placed you in a jail cell along with up to 20 other Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could please take a look at 65 ter 3565. Q. Mr. Osmanovic, if you can take a look at this -- this is actually three photographs. This is the first one. If you can look at this first one. Can you tell us what that is a picture of?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: We see the hallway, identical to the hallway in the police station in Vlasenica, in this part here that I will mark with A is the stairwell. On the right-hand side is a metal door, it used to be the toilet, later turned into a makeshift store-room. On the right-hand side is the door to one of the offices of the fire brigade. And opposite is the door to the section for the IDs and passports. And on the right-hand side we see two toilets.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Very good. And you mentioned that to the right, right next to the stairwell is a door that was a toilet, became a storage room.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could go to the next picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I think that's a better view of that door; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is from another angle. We see the stairwell leading down to the ground floor and up to the second floor, and we see that door.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, by "that door" I take it you're talking about the toilet that became a store-room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And let's enter that room. Could we go to the next picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, do you recognise this room?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: This a cell of a police station in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: When --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what he said at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, could you just repeat what you said at the end of your testimony there. The interpreter didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a cell at the police station. That's the former storage room.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, when you were arrested, is this the cell you were brought to?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Except that this wooden bunk did not exist then. And here, in the upper corner, was a window that you can't see, and it was -- there was brick on the edge.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And how long were you detained in this cell?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: There were two cells like this. One on the ground floor; one upstairs. It was a time when you didn't know when you were awake and you were sleeping. I spent two days in a cell like this before being moved upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement that there was up to 20 grown Muslim men in this cell. How did you all fit in there?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The person who got first to the corner and managed to squat did so. Most of the other people had to stand, and we were packed in like sardines.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now you mentioned -- you mentioned that after a couple of days you were moved to another cell. Where was that cell located?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's just above this one, directly upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Was it similar in size?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Slightly larger.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, this second cell that you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Olmsted. Mr. Osmanovic, I'm trying to get some idea in terms of perspective. From the photograph, we see the width of the cell. Could you tell me -- if you look at the foot of the bunk that's now there, how -- about how near would that have been to the -- to the front end of the cell? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean to the wall?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, to the door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the door to the bunk there could be 80, 90 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Just a follow-up on the Presiding Judge's question, what approximately were the dimensions of the room? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2.5 to 3 metres by 1.80 metres, because it used to be a toilet, later turned into a store-room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, this second jail cell that you were detained in, on the second floor, can you tell us how many days you were in that cell for?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in that cell until the 2nd of June, when I was move to the municipal prison in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And since you're familiar with the interior of the building, how -- where was this cell in relation to the SJB chief's office?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Right opposite his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You mentioned in your prior written statement that Dzemal Ambeskovic was murdered near one of the SJB cells. Can you tell us whether it was a cell on the first floor or on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1043, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, in your prior statements, you name a number of persons who were responsible for the mistreating and interrogating yourself and other Muslims at the SJB building. And I would like to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 2378.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: To see whether you could identify any of the people who were mistreating you at the SJB building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could zoom out and go to page 2 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now this document is entitled: "List of Members the Special Platoon at Vlasenica SJB." Mr. Osmanovic, were you aware back in 1992 that a special unit existed in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, in all fairness it says "List of Members of the Reserve Police Forces." Are you claiming that "special unit" and "reserve police" is one and the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for catching that. Page 2 of the English, please. This is page 1. There we go. Let me ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, were you aware back in 1992 that a special platoon or special unit existed in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, in April, I noticed uniformed men in camouflage uniforms. I thought that they were members of the special military police. However, according to this list that we have here they were members of the special platoon at the police station in Vlasenica, and these are people whom I have named by their first and last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Who was the leader, the commander, of this special platoon?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: When I stayed at Susica camp in Vlasenica, where I stayed, people there would say the prince is coming, the king is coming, the commander is coming; Kraljevic meaning prince. And we have the surname here, it is Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just for the record, is that the person listed as number one on this list?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now I think you've mentioned but just to confirm, are you familiar generally with the persons listed on this document?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm familiar with a quite large number of persons on this list. I know their first names, their last names, I know the names of their parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And what are their ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: They were all of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I want you to focus on the time you were at the SJB building, you and the other Muslims were being detained at the SJB building. And could you tell us from this list whether any persons on this list were involved in either interrogating or mistreating the detainees at that building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes they were. Namely, it was the person under number serial 3, the one under serial number 4, serial number 6, serial number 12, 13, 8, 15, 20, number 23, number 24, 25, the person under the serial -- under serial number 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The person listed under number 23, Dragan Nikolic, who was he back in 1992 -- April 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Until April 1993 he worked in the aluminum factory. In April I saw him once in front of the bauxite mine in Vlasenica. He was armed. There was the Crisis Staff there. Afterwards, he was the commander of the Susica camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's take a look at another list, 65 ter 2815. And while we're doing that, can we mark that last document for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1044, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Osmanovic, with regard to this document which is entitled: "Reserve Workers who Have Worked at the Police Station in September 1992," I'm going ask you the same series of questions. And, first of all, are you familiar generally with the persons who are listed on this document?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know some of the people on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can you tell us what their ethnicities were?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: They were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, again, focussing on your time at SJB building when you were detained there with other Muslims, can you identify any persons on this list who were involved in the interrogation and mistreatment of the Muslims detained there?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The person under number 16, Slavko Garic. Actually, the name here is Slavko but they just mentioned the surname, Garic. I didn't know his first name at the time and he was interrogating people. Then also Sekulic, the person under number 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can I ask you about number 2, Rade Milic. What role did he have in your arrest.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Rade Milic used to be a policeman at the public security on the reserve force in Vlasenica. He lived in my neighbourhood, and he was present when I was taken away from my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That was on the 22nd of May?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could turn to the second page of the B/C/S. I don't think there is a second page for the ... for the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I'll ask you the same question. Can you identify any persons listed here as among the perpetrators of mistreatment of the Muslims detained at SJB.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The person under serial number 56, Zoran Pantic, interrogated people at the police station. Also, the person under 72, Predrag, Basta. Some people in town knew him as Dragan Basta nicknamed Sar. 75, also, Tosa Ostojic [phoen], a retired inspector of the public security station in Vlasenica who interrogated people, and Basta was among the persons took people in, brought them into the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You mentioned that Predrag Basta's nickname was Car. Could you spell that for the record.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is C-a-r.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In English, interpreter's comment: It is T-s-a-r, Tsar.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now number 50, Ljubisa Sekulic. Did you see him at all when you were at the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was the brother German of the first Sekulic who is on the first page. I saw him at the prison, and he was with Cvijetin Ramljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just to clarify, did you also see him at the SJB building, mistreating Muslim detainees?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: He maltreated other people. He did not maltreat me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could just turn to the third page. And I'll ask you the same question, whether you can identify any of the perpetrators at the SJB building, amongst these names?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: 77, Duric Elvis. The person under 79, Sinisa Dosic. Under 81, Goran Pajic. 88, Stupar. The person under 100, serial number 100, Ljubisa Vukotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Under number 92, Goran Tesic. What was he doing back in this time-period, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Goran Tesic got -- was a guard at the Susica camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can we mark this one for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, before you leave this document, I'd like to put a question to Mr. Osmanovic. Namely, the function of these people on the list that we are seeing on the screen in front of us, it says that it's a list of reserve workers and I'm just curious to know what that means. It's quite a comprehensive list, counting more than 100 people and my question is were these people members of the police force or were they were recruited sort of at that moment to assist in running the SJB. What was their function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were not active policemen. They were not employed on a regular basis at the police station. They just appeared at the police station in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And as -- and, as we can see, they were also paid, apparently. What were they paid for; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For some kind of work they did, most probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's cal up one more list. It's 65 ter 2815. Was the last one marked? I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1045.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, my question is why do you want to have this list MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, obviously he's not a member of the police so I was not thinking he would be the appropriate witness to admit it. There will be another witness testifying this week who will authenticate and admit them all.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1045, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, if we could take look at 65 ter 2815. And if you could just flip to page 4. Oh, correction 2814; I apologise. And we can flip ahead to page 4 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now we just looked at a reserve police payroll. Now we're looking at the active police payroll, May 1992. Mr. Osmanovic, are you familiar with the persons listed on this document?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with most -- most of them. But I did not see some of them in the police station as part of active force.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: What are their ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: They're all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm going ask you the same question I asked with regard to the other documents. When you were detained at the SJB building, did you see any of the persons listed here?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I did. I saw a large number of the people on this list. I did not see the three women on the list. But as for the rest, I saw most of them. But I have to note that they behaved in a very professional way, as policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we look at number 20, Sinisa Miljanic. You mention him in your statement when you were detained at SJB building. What was he doing at the building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Miljanic was not on the active force in the -- of the police station. Until April 1992, he belonged to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- I believe somewhere in your statement when you're talking about what happened at the SJB building, you mentioned him. If you could just tell the Trial Chamber what you saw him doing when you were being detained at the SJB building.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was detained at the police station in Vlasenica. Miljanic took us out to put the body of Dzemal Vlaskovic [as interpreted] who was killed there near the police station at Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure she heard the witness correctly. If he could repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, I don't think the interpreter heard the name of the person whose body you took out of the SJB. Could you repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dzemal Ambeskovic is the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, in your October 1994 statement, you state that a person by the name of Stevan Mumovic was responsible for killing Ambeskovic. What kind of uniform was Mumovic wearing?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Stevan Mumovic, who was from Racica [phoen] village in the Han Pijesak municipality, was a convict of the Foca prison for a very long time. He was serving time because he had killed a Muslim. He came to Vlasenica in 1992. He had a camouflage uniform on on the sleeve of which was written "war police" on the patch.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you know what the difference between war police and reserve police is?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: War police is something that I saw for the very first time written on the patch op his sleeve.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could look at number 24, Goran Deuric. Did he play any role in your arrest?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: He too was a reserve policeman up to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And what role did he play in your arrest?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: He was just there to escort me to the police station. He was present when I was taken in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And number 25, Branislav Sokanovic. Who was he back in May/June 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sokanovic, and then number 25, was the prison governor, the prison warden, but he was not from Vlasenica. This person's conduct was markedly professional while he was in the building of the municipal prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May we have that marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1046, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, I'm just slightly confused about what these people were doing, because Mr. Osmanovic made reference to the municipal prison. And -- and on the list it appears that these were active policemen working at the Vlasenica SJB. So my question is: Were these running the prison at the SJB station itself or were they manning or guarding the municipal prison. And where was that located, if not in the SJB itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In fact we're going move to municipal prison right now. Just to clarify, as I understand his testimony we just talked about this Sokanovic who was the prison warden. Up to this point we have been talking about the SJB building itself and the jail cells located at that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's move on to the prison, the municipal prison, which according to your testimony you were taken to after you were detained at the SJB building. Could you tell us approximately how far the municipal prison is from the SJB building.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The municipal prison is between 200 and 250 metres from the SJB. The prison was right behind the court building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And who took you to the prison?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Miljanic did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And approximately how many days were you detained at the municipal prison?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I was there from the 2nd of June until the 17th or the 18th of June, when I was transferred to the Susica camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And while you were being detained at the municipal prison, who is guarding you and other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The guards guarding us were men of Serb ethnicity. Some of them are on this list of reserve policemen of the SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you give us their names.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Sekulic brothers, Dusan Duric, aka Pikusa, Cvijetin Ramljak, Slobodan Tesic. There were also some other people whom I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did you see Predrag Basta at all while you were detained at the municipal prison?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Basta would come occasionally to the municipal prison. Excuse me, on the 2nd of June, people were rounded up in Vlasenica and the surrounding villages, and they were taken away. Regrettably, some of them never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And just to clarify: Were they taken away from? Were they taken away from the prison or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were taken away from the municipal prison in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, in your prior statements, you talk about how you were -- you and other detainees were mistreated by some of the guards at the municipal prison. Can you tell us which guards were beating or otherwise abusing the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The prisoners at the municipal prison in Vlasenica were mistreated and maltreated. Actually, the maltreatment included deprivation of food and water and beating. Among those who particularly mistreated the prisoners were Ramljak and Djuric who worked in one shift. Then Sekulic and Tesic, they worked in another shift. Now, as regards Tesic he was not that perverted; whereas, Sekulic actually viciously treated some people. They would bring from the nearby cafe, which was called Excalibur and which was of 50 metres from the building, anyone who wanted to beat the inmates. They even brought children. Different people came in. The door would just swing open from civilians to uniformed people, known and unknown people. Anyone could come in. The guards provided no protection at all, no refuge at all to the inmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You mentioned in your prior statement that while you were detained at the municipal prison, at one point you were taken out of the prison to collect bodies, 22 bodies, and bury them from the village of Drum.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we can take a look at 65 ter 3569. And if he can use the electronic pen for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, taking a look at this photograph in front of you, can you see the Vlasenica SJB building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The building of the public security station is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we are going to have to keep it zoomed out so that you can mark on it, but could you put a number 1 on the SJB?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The building of the public security is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The usher is going to help you mark it on the screen. Could you please put a number ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Okay. I have been informed that you have marked it number 1. Could you circle the village of Drum, just put a big circle around this village of Drum on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far the village of Drum is from the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: 1 and a half kilometres to 2, maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, you're familiar with the interior of the SJB building. If I was standing in the SJB chief's office on the second floor looking out the window, would I be able to see the village of Drum?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Drum to collect the bodies, where were the bodies located?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The bodies were at Nezir's Cafe. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you mark that with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And where did you bury them?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: We buried them at the entrance to the Muslim cemetery called Rakita.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you put a number 3 where that's located.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now did you know any of the victims, any of the people who -- whose bodies you collected that day?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: What were their ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: They were all Muslim. Because in the Drum village there were only two Serb houses, the house belonging to a haulier at the very entrance to the village, and another house belonging to somebody called Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Were any members of the special police unit present while you were collecting and burying these bodies?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Zoran Obrenovic was there. Then the worker of the public utility enterprise, Pecenica. There was Stupar. We had take off jewellery from the dead bodies, rings, any valuables, and then we had to line them into a big grave that had been dug already.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this into evidence, this picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P1047, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's move on to your detention at Susica camp --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted. Mr. Witness, the victims, were they all men or were they men and women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were all men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's move on to your detention at Susica camp in June 1992. Do you recall who transported you from the municipal prison to the Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: From the municipal prison in Vlasenica to the Susica camp, I and others with me were transferred by Predrag Basta, nicknamed Car, in his own privately owned truck, Zastava 650 was the make.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And in your prior statements, you describe a number of incidents of beatings and killings of the Muslim detainees at Susica camp. Could you tell us whether any members of the special police unit or reserve police were involved in those beatings and killings?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: On this list, on the second list, there are a few names. Dragan Nikolic, nicknamed Jenki, he was the fear of the entire Susica camp. The dread and terror of the camp. Other members from this list, and yet others who are not on the list also came to the camp. Goran Viskovic, nicknamed Vjetar, Wind, is on this list. He came wearing a helmet like a construction worker, and he himself had inscribed UN on the helmet. We only prayed to God for dawn to come, because every night the same thing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just to clarify: The list you're looking at, is that the special police platoon list?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran Obrenovic or Sladan Pajic at Susica camp abusing detainees?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw both Sladan and Zoran, Duric brothers Aco and Elvis. I also saw Mr. Vukotic who had brought people from Suljkovic [phoen] neighbourhood. Ljubisa Vukotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, were other members of your family detained at Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Out of my family, two of us brothers, my mother, and two sisters were at the camp. At the police station, my elder brother remained after we left for the camp. Later, he was under house arrest with an obligation to report to the police station every 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: How long was your brother detained at Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: My brother never left Susica, unfortunately. He was found in a mass grave in Kljestani, decapitated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: How long did your sisters remain at Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: My elder sister, Fatima was sent to Cerska, and then my mother, Fata followed her to Cerska; whereas, my sister Ferida stayed on. She was found burnt in the Pelemis camp, burned to death.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to -- and I'm sorry for having to bring that up. But if we can move on -- are you okay, Mr. Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to Batkovic camp. Do you recall seeing any members of the Vlasenica special police unit at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Under what circumstances did you see members of the special unit at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I was transferred to Batkovic, towards the end of June, and sometime in August, or, rather, in September a group of people was brought in. They had been intercepted somewhere in an attempt, perhaps, to get to the free territory. Some of them had been in Milici prison, others in Vlasenica prison, and that was the last group that came from Vlasenica. At that time, there was Sekulic, Pajic, Obrenovic. My sister-in-law and Obrenovic were family, in-laws because my brother was married to his cousin. I asked if my parents were still alive, and he said, unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you recall while you were at Batkovic seeing other members of the civilian police at that camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian police from Bijeljina municipality came to take inmates out for labour duty. They would work in Semberija and Sava companies, in the wire factory, at the sugar refinery. That's where regular police used to take people. As for labour, digging trenches and making defence lines and felling trees for the first front line, more -- that's when troops, army troops would come to take inmates out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: When you referred to army troops, do you mean the VRS army?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can we look at 65 ter 1329. And if we could go to page 148 in the B/C/S. 148. Unfortunately, the English is not a complete translation so maybe just stay on the first page for the English but go to 148 for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, Mr. Osmanovic, you reviewed this document - it's quite a long document - and you reviewed it during proofing yesterday. But prior to reviewing it yesterday, had you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, what is this? And who drew up this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We -- after the witness testifies, I can probably provide a little more details as to where the list comes from. He is going to authenticate it to a certain degree. I'm sorry, there is just going to be a page correction. The page is 138; I apologise. If we could scroll down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, do you see your name anywhere on this list?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, number 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Is this information accurate with regard to your detention at Batkovic camp in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, when you reviewed this rather long list, were you able to recognise any other persons listed?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised people from Vlasenica by name and surname. I recognised some people who were with me in the same labour groups. They were from Zvornik, Kalesija, and Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Were all these people at Batkovic camp with you?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Approximately, roughly how many names could you recognise on this list?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: As for Vlasenica municipality or the town of Vlasenica, I know everyone down to the last man. As for the others, I know only those who worked with me in the same labour groups from other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May we mark this document for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1048, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I just have one more document to show you, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could 65 ter 3563 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: During your proofing yesterday, Mr. Osmanovic, did you have the opportunity to review this document which is the crime register from Vlasenica SJB?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And as you reviewed this register, were you able to identify among the persons reported in this register Bosniaks who were at detention facilities with you in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A certain number of persons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now if we could look at 65 ter 10288. Yes, and I'll indicate that this document is another document that we created during his proofing yesterday, so it wasn't on the original list. It's just been loaded into e-court, and, like I said, it was signed by the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, did you sign -- is this statement signed by you?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, we see here listed seven names. Are these people that could you identify that were at detention facilities, along with you, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd like to tender this into evidence. Obviously, it's not on our 65 ter list but because it was created yesterday during proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is there any objection? Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1049, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And since we've taken a look at 65 ter 3563, the crime register, could we have that marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 1050, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. The -- we are so near the break that I would -- probably wait until we return for cross-examination to begin. So we resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Osmanovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My name is Slobodan Cvijetic. I am co-counsel on the Defence team of the accused Mico Stanisic. I have just a few questions for you. I've read all your statements, and I believe you did not touch upon one of the subjects that you had covered earlier today. I would like turn your attention to the takeover of power in Vlasenica municipality, and you will help me with the dates. So you maintain that on this one day the JNA turned up and took control of all the most important state institutions; correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You'll have to wait for me to finish my question and make a second's pause before you answer, because the interpreters are not going to be able to follow otherwise. Could you tell us in a few sentences what it looked like?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992, there was a takeover of power in Vlasenica municipality. They took control of all the most important institutions, such as the court, the town hall, the bank, various companies. Armed people of Serb ethnicity from Vlasenica turned out in the street, wearing rifles and standard army weapons. Six armoured vehicles, including tanks, were also parked next to the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you notice a paramilitary unit that also appeared in the street at the time?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paramilitary units, that is army units, they were all armed. Some of them wore traditional olive-green uniforms, others camouflage uniforms, and they were all armed. There were paramilitary units wearing different insignia. Some of them had eagles on their caps. Some of them had the tricolour on the cap. Some of them had nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: A paramilitary unit from Sekovici is mentioned. Do you know anything about them?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: That paramilitary unit from Sekovici, sir, they were all armed. They were all uniformed. They were acting as one team, men wearing different insignia were moving together. I don't see any difference between various paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I don't see any paramilitary unit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the police station building was also taken control of, and all the policemen, both Serbs and Muslims, were disarmed during this takeover of power?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In your earlier statements, you did not identify the person who drove that Volkswagen Golf. You just said that this vehicle had a megaphone inviting Muslims to turn over weapons.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Who drove that vehicle from which this proclamation was read, I don't know. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In response to a question from the Prosecutor, and perhaps Judge Harhoff asked about it as well, you said that you had noticed also a reserve police unit, and you named some of the people you knew. Was that the first time you saw them in uniform?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any idea who could have mobilised them and armed them?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbian Municipality of Vlasenica, the police station of Vlasenica, and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. A police station cannot conduct mobilisation. There is a specific authority in the municipality in charge of mobilisation; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: There is the National Secretariat for Defence. There was a National Secretariat for Defence which conducted mobilisation of the reserve forces for the benefit of the then-Territorial Defence; whereas, the police force mobilised their own reserve, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, that's your opinion. We can't agree on that. I think you said something about the role of the Crisis Staff in those times. Do you know when it was established who was the president and what were the competences of that Crisis Staff? Just slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff of Vlasenica Municipality, now, I saw two orders of this Crisis Staff. One was hanging outside a company, a business, in writing, that was the furniture factory. And the other order was verbal, demanding that everyone go back to work, to the Serbian Municipality of Vlasenica, those who had fled but were still there, and in my view, the Crisis Staff was the agency that governed Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, I'm just going through your statement where you say that in -- during those days the Crisis Staff was the main authority in Vlasenica municipality. I think you dealt, in your statement, also with the appointment of the chief of police, Mr. Bjelanovic, and you related that to the decisions of the Crisis Staff. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, you're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What is right then?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelanovic was the chief of the police station in Vlasenica when the first multi-party elections took place, whereas, the commander of the police station was Mr. Turkovic. Because one post belonged to the SDA and the other post to the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned this person Kraljevic, nicknamed Kralj, king. You mentioned him in relation to the work and operation of the Susica camp; correct? You said that -- in fact, you claim that he had the rank of the lieutenant in the Yugoslav People's Army, right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kraljevic, if I should call him mister at all, I mentioned in my story about Susica camp where this Nikolic, nicknamed Jenki, said that we had to clean the perimeter because Kraljevic, the commander, the prince, was coming. And when Major Vlasic [as interpreted] asked, he said that he was responsible only to Kraljevic because Kraljevic was the commander -- his commander. Mico Kraljevic still lives in Vlasenica and work there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by your statement where you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the Prosecutor on his foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, just a clarification. I think -- the transcript says "Major Vlasic." I think that was not the name that he gave. I -- obviously I don't understand B/C/S, but I think, just knowing the witness's statement, that he meant someone else. Perhaps you could seek a clarification on the person who said that he was only responsible to Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The witness can repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: At the Susica camp when Kraljevic was coming driving the car of Mustafa Jasarevic, Dragan Nikolic used to say, The king was coming; the commander was coming. The camp must be cleaned. When Veljko Basic came with a list - and he was a major wearing a uniform of the JNA - Nikolic said only Kraljevic is my commander. I'm responsible only to him, no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You identified Dragan Nikolic as a worker of the Alpro factory, as an alcoholic, and it is written here also that you saw him and considered him to be a member of the Serbian special military police?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: As for Dragan Nikolic, nicknamed Jenki he was known to the entire town of Vlasenica as a man who was very given to drinking. This is a person who worked together with my brother in the aluminum pressings factory in Vlasenica. And this is a person whom I saw twice: Once outside the Crisis Staff in Vlasenica, which was in the administration building of the bauxite mine in Vlasenica, and the second time, when I was transferred to the Susica camp where he was lord and master and laid down the law. Just to clarify, sir, when you refer to special military police I never before had occasion to see the police wearing camouflage uniforms. I only knew that the army wore such uniforms, that's why I thought that he was a member of the army special police. But I, yesterday, saw on the list that he was a member of the special platoon of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But he was wearing an army camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing an army camouflage uniform. He was armed with a 7.62-millimetre pistol. He has a knife, a bayonet which was used on an M48 rifle. He a defensive and offensive hand grenade, and he also had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution has shown you this list of, so to speak, regular policemen are -- in the police station, and you said that they professionally discharged their duties. I noticed on that list that the only one who did not receive his salary was precisely this Sokanovic person who you say you later noticed was in charge of the prison.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: In Vlasenica I did not know any policeman by the name of Sokanovic. As a matter of fact, there are some names that are unfamiliar to me on this list. This man came to the prison, municipal prison in Vlasenica. He said that he was the warden. His conduct was extremely professional and fair towards everybody, irrespective of sex, of age, of anything. He was quite professional. When I went -- was transferred to the Susica camp, I saw a number of people there and one of them was Daniel Sokanovic who hailed from Zenica. How he came to be in that camp, I don't know, but he said that he had worked in the central prison in Sarajevo before. But this was a person who was extremely fair and correct in his treatment of other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also referred to a Stevan Mumovic who you claim killed this Beskovic [as interpreted]; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Stevan Mumovic killed Ferid Binic [phoen]. Stevan Mumovic was a long time convict of the Foca prison. He hailed from the village of Racica, the Han Pijesak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm wrong because you have those lists. I didn't find him on any list.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't identify him on any list either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness's answer is indicated as a question. That should be corrected. I'm not quite sure what line that is. It is line 14, line 14. On this page. Well, the question and answer -- anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: He is not on any of these lists?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, in March 1992, did the Muslim population organise itself in any paramilitary way in that area, municipality of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that in Vlasenica municipality and in the town proper Serbs and Muslims socialised. They stood guard together in the streets. They had armed and unarmed patrols. I heard that there was some sort of a check-point in the Drum village area. I'm not sure whether they were armed. That is in March. As regards April, the former local commune of Cerska put up an armed resistance to the Serb forces, and they managed to hold out in their homes until February 1993. As for some paramilitary organisations, I was not aware of the existence of any.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not going to dwell on Batkovic because it is Vlasenica that we're interested in. But as regards Batkovic, you told us that it was precisely three Muslim guards who mistreated the inmates the most.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You were exchanged for civilians. Can you relate that for us in brief?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of July, 1993, in the morning, we were loaded onto buses at Batkovic, and we were taken to the village of Jablanica, that is the Lopare municipality. From where we proceeded on foot to descend into the village of Sibosnica where at a football pitch, we parted. Some went in one direction, others in another direction. There were representatives of the municipalities from the Vlasenica area. I recognised Bajo, he used to play football. He was there on the Serbs. When I passed through the area under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, civilian Serbs were passing in the other direction and they were not in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, I -- this concludes my questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No question for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, you mentioned someone by the name of Veljko Basic at Susica camp. Could you tell us, what was his position prior to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Veljko Basic was a retired policeman of the public security in Vlasenica. He arrived at Susica camp with some sort of a list, reading out -- for the names of those people who are to be exchanged to be read out. I asked Veljko since I know him, I knew him, whether Hajrudin, my brother, and I could go together. And he said to me, no. You will go and he will remain here as security that you will not escape. Regrettably, my brother was found three years ago decapitated. His head was found several months ago on the 24th of April in fact, and that was the kind of guarantee that I got from Veljko. By the way, the head of my brother was found 25 kilometres distant, as the crow flies, from his body. The body was found at Kljestani and the head at the Debelo Brdo -- in the Debelo Brdo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You answered some questions about armed resistance in Vlasenica municipality. Mr. Osmanovic, could you tell us whether there was any armed resistance in Vlasenica town itself?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in Vlasenica, there was no armed resistance whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: In the days surrounding the takeover of Vlasenica town by the Serb forces, did you have a chance to observe what the civilian police were doing in the municipality when these paramilitaries and other groups were taking over the municipality?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment of the takeover of the municipality of Vlasenica, I didn't see any of that. When I went to work, I saw very -- a very small number of active policemen just in passing. I saw, however, larger numbers of armed men of Serb ethnicity who were on duty at the cross-roads, in the factories, and who moved about town. They all had a patch, or, rather, a ribbon on their right sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Are you aware of any efforts by the police in Vlasenica to arrest these paramilitary groups that were taking over the town?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such efforts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Osmanovic. Just one little question for clarification. The persons who were taking part in the mistreatment at the Batkovic camp, you mentioned that three of them were of Muslim ethnicity. And my question is: What was their function? Were they employed with the police or were they -- what were they doing there, and how come they would beat up their fellow ethnicity brothers, if I may say so?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, upon my arrival at Susica camp, I found Dzemal Zahirovic, called Spajzer, who had been taken to the camp, Batkovic camp, before me, two days before me. When I arrived he was already commanding a group of inmates who were actually erecting a fence around the compound. In the meantime, a group also arrived from Brezevo Polje, Brcko municipality, among who was a name -- a man by the name of Fikret Smajlovic, nicknamed Piklic in camouflage uniform, and the very moment he arrived he started ordering people about as to who would do what, who would go with who. But who had appointed him to that post I really don't know. After a certain time, another group of inmates was brought including man in camouflage uniform named Bekric. He joined the first two men, Bekric kicked people. Smajlovic used a cable which he called an American stick. And he also used the metal buckle of his belt whereas Zahirovic -- Zahirovic who was a Roma person, he used primitive instruments so to speak. He used stones, poles, whatever he could lay his hands on. These three men, this group that I am mentioning, beat most viciously the group which was called the special group, include -- which included Muslims and Croats. One of them was Nedim Mostarcevic who was from Tuzla, who was brought there -- who was brought wounded. He was called beret 1. Fadil Alihodzic, who was called beret 2, who was captured at the line. He is from Vlasenica and I know him well. There were two Croats and an Albanian who managed to escape the Batkovic camp and reach Brezevo Polje, but they were caught and returned. They were accorded what was referred to as special treatment by these three. They were not given any food or any water, and they were beaten every day, literally every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you for this response. I'm still curious to know the reason to know why, if you can tell us, some of the inmates became engaged in beating other inmates. Were they ordered to do by the camp, the leadership of the camp, the camp commander or -- how did this come about?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now who ordered it, I don't know. But I know that these people had a privileged position, all three of them. Smajlovic even had his own private car, Yugo, parked outside the hangar. He came and went as he pleased outside the compound which other people were not able to do. He held himself as a person who had the right to command everyone within the compound. Zahirovic within the confines of the camp did not go outside to work anywhere, but he decided within the compound who should go in which group and do what; whereas, Bekric led a group that went out to loot Muslim villages in the vicinity of Bijeljina, Akmacici, Janjari, and another village. They would take out home appliances, TV sets, whatever they found. So they held a privileged position, but who ordered them to treat people that way, their own compatriots, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I may have misunderstood, but am I correct in assuming that these three gentlemen were not themselves inmates in the camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: They were prisoners. They slept in the same place as us but they acted as bosses in the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And yet they could leave the camp as they pleased?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Smajlovic could leave the camp whenever he wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours in this context just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Were there such privileged Muslims at the Susica camp as well?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a number of privileged people appointed by Dragan Nikolic in the Susica camp as well, but they did not beat others. They were like on duty. They designated people who should go out to work, but they did not beat people unlike the other ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we thank you, sir, for coming to assist the Tribunal, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home. We note the personal indignities [realtime transcript read in error "insignificant knits"] and discomfort, to put it mildly, that you would have suffered, and we empathise with you. So we thank you for your assistance to us. Thank you, sir. You are now released as a witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, according to the schedule that we were to received [sic], your next witness is scheduled -- is not scheduled to begin until tomorrow. Having regard to the early hour at which this witness has concluded in his testimony, are you in a position to begin the testimony of that witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, unfortunately, I don't think we are. We did anticipate that the cross-examination would go two hours as they had -- the Defence had indicated. And the witness just arrived last night, and needed proofing today, reviewing his statements and such. And if we could resume tomorrow, that would be ideal for us. I think we'll still be on schedule for this week though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I have one question to avoid eventually problems with the numbering of the exhibited documents. The package when it was tendered was given one number, P1041. Madam Registrar, do all the nine documents then get dot 1, 2, 3, et cetera, numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, the package is numbered 1041.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- through 1041.08, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the last one is then?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last one is --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last one is document 2280.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There was an additional statement that was submitted as Rule 65 ter 102 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's included -- THE REGISTRAR. -- 06.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the other additional statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- 10288 was a separate document, which has received Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 49, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- exhibit number 1049, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. But then 2280 is the annotated one that has -- that is in the package?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 2280 is an aerial photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Annotated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is one annotated photograph which was 65 ter exhibit 2281.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which is exhibit number 1042.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 42. Okay. And then one last -- one thing more. P1045 should be MFI'd which is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just to be sure.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we rise, I note for the record that page 41, line 17, I'm recorded as noting "the personal insignificant knits and discomfort." What the record should show is that I noted the personal indignities and discomfort suffered by the witness. Thank you. Is anybody in a position to volunteer information, from either side, as to what progress you have made, you plural, have made in the representations that would have to be formally put to the President as to the site visit?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have any information in regard to that. I know Ms. Korner has had some discussion with the Defence about that. I think they're coming up with a couple different plans. I don't know where that is in the process, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: May I just add in this connection that it takes a couple of months, at least, to prepare a site visit. So if we are scheduling a site visit before the summer recess, then time is beginning to -- to -- to get short. So, as I said, if we are to carry on with these plans, then we must hear from the parties very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may, then on the same topic, Your Honour, we were discussed this issue with -- yeah. We will discuss this -- discuss this issue with our colleagues from the OTP, and we -- we -- we actually -- I would say made a proposal regarding the schedules and -- and places to visit, et cetera, and I believe that during this day, you will have detailed information about that. Our friends from Prosecution are taking care about the -- because they were a part of -- of -- of same -- same -- I would say site visit before, so they will classify everything, and I believe that during day, at latest tomorrow, you will have detailed information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't promised detailed information as of tomorrow, but I will speak with Ms. Korner today, and we will report back to you where we are tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we resume in this courtroom at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
